annotationRationale: The question combines equal-distance symmetry with logarithmic operations. The primary method determines the product directly; the alternative explicitly finds both solutions using absolute-value branches. Logarithm definitions support both routes.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The required positive values are 25 and 81/25, whose product is 81, choice E. Equivalently, their logarithms are symmetric about log_6 9, so their product is 9². The stem, choices and key are consistent; no figure is needed.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods were supplied. AoPS Solutions 1 and 2 are retained in symmetric-logarithms. LIVE and AoPS Solution 3 are retained in absolute-value-branches. These provide a useful direct-product argument and an independently complete explicit solution of both branches.
review.annotationCheck: Absolute-value geometry and logarithmic operations correctly identify the main work. Logarithm definitions appropriately support domain restrictions and uniqueness. The branch-solving procedure is correctly recorded locally through cnm_008. No inherited shared-method provenance is applicable.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The fixed distance d is strictly positive because log_6 10>1. Exactly two logarithm values occur, log_6 9±d, each corresponding to one positive solution. Adding them gives log_6(ab)=2log_6 9=log_6 81, hence ab=81.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The AoPS reference and sourceMethod accurately credit Solutions 1 and 2 for this question. The explanation uses original prose and explicitly supplies domain, distinctness and completeness checks. source-informed-original correctly reflects third-party provenance.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first sentence explains why symmetry avoids computing the distance. The positivity of d and the one-to-one logarithm correspondence justify exactly two solutions, and the product-rule transition is clear.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_007 covers equal-distance geometry, cnm_h043 supports logarithm meaning and uniqueness, and cnm_h044 covers the product and power rules. Every immediate ID is used.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The fixed distance is log_6(5/3), so twice it is log_6(25/9)>0. The two absolute-value branches give x/9=25/9 or 9/25, hence x=25 or 81/25. Both satisfy the positive domain, and their product is 81.
